messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Hospital Course:
The patient presented with altered mental status, visual disturbances, and seizures associated with a rash and polyarthralgia. She was found to have hypertension and polysubstance abuse. Antinuclear antibodies (ANA) and double-stranded deoxyribonuclease (dsDNA) antibodies were both positive, and C3 and C4 complement factors were low. The patient was diagnosed with SLE and started on methylprednisolone pulse therapy due to active proliferative lupus nephritis. Her kidney function and arthralgia improved, and she was transitioned to oral prednisone taper. Mycophenolate mofetil was also started, and pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP) prophylaxis was given. The patient's hospital stay was significant for treatment of SLE related manifestations and hypertension. 
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Disposition:
The patient was discharged home with close follow-up with her primary care physician and rheumatologist for continuation of management of her SLE and hypertension. 

Instructions:
The patient is advised to continue medications as prescribed and report any adverse effects to her physician. She should monitor her blood pressure and follow a low-sodium diet. She should avoid sun exposure and use sunscreen for protection. The patient is to have close follow-up with her physician for monitoring of her kidney function and disease activity. 

Follow-Up:
Urgent follow-up is recommended with the primary care physician and rheumatologist within one week.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The admission was chiefly for newly diagnosed systemic lupus erythematosus with organ involvement: proliferative lupus nephritis, neuropsychiatric features, rash and arthritis, treated with pulse steroids and mycophenolate. This belongs to chapter M (musculoskeletal and connective tissue). The category is M32, systemic lupus erythematosus.

CODE: M32
